data.name: About_Tagline
data.value: Modern fork of x360ce, rebuilt with SDL3, WPF and .NET 10

data.name: About_Description
data.value: PadForge turns any input device into any virtual controller. Gamepads, joysticks, keyboards, mice and touchscreens are mapped to virtual game controllers (Xbox, PlayStation, flight sticks, wheels, third-party gamepads) or keyboard+mouse / MIDI output that games treat as real hardware. Powered by HIDMaestro and Windows MIDI Services. It uses SDL3 for controller input, Windows Raw Input for keyboard and mouse, HidHide for per-game device masking, and provides a modern Fluent Design interface for mapping, deadzones, sensitivity curves and force feedback.

data.name: Pad_Audio_BufferLength_Tooltip
data.value: Advanced. Sets the Bluetooth audio buffer this controller uses for speaker sound, haptics and microphone capture together, not the speaker alone. Lower values cut the delay on all three and leave less room for Bluetooth timing to wobble, so dropouts become more likely. 48 is the default, which is what the reference implementation ships. Measured on one setup: about 223 ms of speaker delay at 255, 110 ms at 64 and 70 ms at 32, with frequent dropouts appearing at 16. Somewhere around 32 to 64 is a practical starting point, but the right value depends on your adapter and surroundings. Takes effect a few seconds after you change it.

While enabled, this device's Pressure mapping sources read no touch as 0%, a resting touch as the Touch Pressure Level and a pad click as 100%.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_SyntheticPressureEnabled_Tooltip
data.value: Shapes this device's Pressure mapping sources into three steps: no touch reads 0%, a resting touch reads the Touch Pressure Level, and clicking the pad reads 100%. Off by default, which keeps raw readings on pads with true analogue pressure.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_MouseMomentum_Tooltip
data.value: The cursor keeps travelling after you lift your finger and coasts to a stop, like a trackball.

data.name: Settings_GyroDeadZone_Tooltip
data.value: Minimum rotation rate (degrees per second) below which gyro output is treated as zero. Rejects at-rest hand tremor without snapping behaviour. Rates past the threshold pass through with the threshold subtracted.

data.name: Pad_Gyro_Subtitle
data.value: Tune how this pad's motion sensor drives mouse and stick output. Calibrate on a flat surface to zero at-rest drift, then dial in sensitivity, smoothing and engage rules to taste.

data.name: Settings_MotionGrip_Tooltip
data.value: How the controller is held. Pointing keeps the frame the driver delivers, a Wii Remote aimed at the screen. Sideways is the remote turned flat with its top edge to the left and the face still up, the NES-style hold. Wii Wheel is the top edge to the left with the face turned towards you, the wheel shell’s hold. Upright is the remote pointed at the ceiling. Each rotates the gyro, the accelerometer and gravity together, for mappings and for the motion the virtual controller reports. The D-pad follows the same frame, so Up is up in the hold.

data.name: Pad_Gyro_Compass_Description
data.value: This controller carries a magnetometer. Anchoring the yaw to magnetic north removes slow horizontal drift from gyro aiming. Calibrate first: press Calibrate, rotate the controller through all orientations in a figure of eight for a few seconds, then press again.

data.name: Settings_GyroCompassYaw_Tooltip
data.value: Adds a small corrective rate that pulls the horizontal aim towards the magnetic heading, so drift cannot accumulate. Requires a stored magnetometer calibration. Samples disturbed by nearby metal or magnets are rejected automatically.

data.name: Pad_Gyro_Grip_WiiWheel
data.value: Wii Wheel, Face Towards You

data.name: Pad_Gyro_Grip_Subtitle
data.value: How the controller is held. Rotates the gyro, the accelerometer and gravity together, for mappings and for the motion the virtual controller reports. The D-pad follows the same frame, so Up is up in the hold.

data.name: Pad_GyroTilt_Subtitle
data.value: Envelope for the Gyro Tilt X / Gyro Tilt Y inputs: hold a tilt and the stick holds its deflection, like Steam's Joystick Deflection mode. Full deflection at the range you set here; Gyro Recentre re-zeroes the resting grip. Yaw (turning the controller flat) is invisible to gravity and does not move these inputs.

data.name: Pad_StickMomentum_Tooltip
data.value: Trackball mode: flick the stick and release, and the cursor keeps travelling, coasting to a stop. Moving the stick again catches it.

data.name: Mapping_MouseCursorSensitivity_Tooltip
data.value: Per-source cursor sensitivity. 1.0 reaches full stick deflection at 10% of screen width from centre. Values above 1.0 reach full deflection with less cursor travel. Values below 1.0 need more.

data.name: Mapping_Sensitivity_Tooltip
data.value: Per-source sensitivity for a plain axis, slider or gamepad stick / trigger. 1.0 leaves the input unchanged. Values above 1.0 reach full deflection with less travel. Values below 1.0 need more.

data.name: Macro_AppVolumeHint
data.value: Controls the volume of a specific application in the Windows volume mixer, scaled to the volume limit. Enter the process name (visible in Task Manager). Use with "Always" trigger, or a button/axis trigger with "While Held" + "Until Release".

data.name: Macro_MouseMoveHint
data.value: Continuously maps the selected axis to mouse movement (or scroll). Use with "Always" trigger, or a button/axis trigger with "While Held" + "Until Release". For stick-to-mouse, create two actions: one for X axis, one for Y axis.

data.name: Pad_Shift_Delay_Tooltip
data.value: How long the input must stay held before the layer reacts. For Hold mode this is a debounce. For Toggle, Latch and Sticky it makes the switch a long press: the layer flips once when the hold crosses this time, and a shorter tap does nothing. 0 reacts instantly.

data.name: Pad_Shift_CycleIncludeBase_Tooltip
data.value: When on, the unshifted Base is a stop in the rotation, so cycling can land back on it. When off, the cursor stays on the ticked layers and you return to Base with a separate activator.

data.name: Pad_Shift_KindAxis_Subtitle
data.value: Engages while an analogue axis is past the threshold value.

data.name: Pad_Shift_PostponeMapping_Tooltip
data.value: When ticked, the activator button still drives any row that uses it as a source. One press both changes layer and fires the button's own mapping. When unticked (default), the activator press is consumed by the layer change only.

data.name: Pad_Shift_InheritUnmapped_Tooltip
data.value: When ticked, targets this layer doesn't explicitly map fall through to the Base layer. When unticked (default), the layer replaces Base entirely and unmapped targets stay off.

data.name: Settings_FlickSnapStrength_Tooltip

data.name: Pad_Steering_LockFeedback_Subtitle
data.value: When a stick set to a steering mode is turned all the way to full lock, play a cue (rumble, trigger or lightbar) so you feel the limit. All off by default.

data.name: Pad_Pointer_Mode_Tooltip
data.value: How the aim drives the OS cursor. Mouse points absolutely. FPS Mouse turns the offset from screen centre into smooth cursor velocity. The border modes confine the cursor to a 4:3 or 16:9 region and pin it to the border while you aim outside it.

data.name: MacroAction_PointerModeCycle_Tooltip
data.value: Advances the Wii pointer mode through the modes selected below for every IR-capable remote on the slot. Each fire moves to the next ticked mode. The cycle position is per-action and resets on app restart.

data.name: Macro_PointerCycleModes_Hint
data.value: Pick which pointer modes the macro should cycle through. Each fire advances to the next ticked mode.

data.name: Pad_Audio_Macros_Desc
data.value: Sounds are played by macros: a trigger (button press, release, hold or formula) plus a Play Sound action. Build them here or on the Macros tab. Delays, repeats and toggles all work.

data.name: Pad_Audio_ToneFilter_Tooltip
data.value: What happens to tones above the limit. High-pitched beeps can be cut off, or folded down an octave at a time so they keep their character at a lower pitch. Folding is recommended. Applies to mirrored audio, macro sounds and the test tone.

data.name: Menu_ChooseIcon_Tip
data.value: Choose this cell's icon: an emoji, an entry from an icon package or an image file.

data.name: RemoteLink_IdentityDescription
data.value: How this PC's pairing identity is stored. Choose a portable mode to carry your pairings on a USB stick between machines.

data.name: About_NAudioDesc
data.value: WASAPI loopback capture for the controller-audio mirror and the audio-bass trigger rumble. NAudio.Midi, which PadForge does not ship, is also the reference for the legacy MIDI API’s WinMM declarations and port sequences, for the rule that a Note On with velocity 0 is a Note Off and for the on/off controllers such as sustain. By Mark Heath. MIT.

data.name: About_VoskDesc
data.value: Offline speech recogniser that hears voice macro phrases. By Alpha Cephei. The model ships inside PadForge. Apache-2.0.

data.name: About_BouncyCastleDesc
data.value: Cryptography for Remote Link pairing and transport (X25519, Ed25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305). Bouncy Castle Licence, an MIT-style licence.

data.name: About_NefariusDevMgmtDesc
data.value: Driver-store install, Bluetooth class filter registration and USB port cycling for the in-app BthPS3 setup and for releasing a hidden USB controller, by nefarius. MIT.

data.name: About_JoyShockMapperDesc
data.value: Winding-angle steering and lean maths, by JibbSmart and Electronicks. MIT.

data.name: About_SteamControllerSingerDesc
data.value: Steam Controller (2015) haptic report layout and note-period maths, by Pila and Roboron3042. BSD 3-Clause.

data.name: About_SteamHapticsSingerDesc
data.value: Steam Controller 2026 and Steam Deck LFO-tone haptic layout, by Pila, Crazy and AAGaming. BSD 3-Clause.

data.name: About_ProtobufNetDesc
data.value: Protocol Buffers serialiser SteamKit2 uses for the Steam wire protocol, by Marc Gravell. Apache-2.0.

data.name: About_Ds4WindowsDesc
data.value: DualShock behaviour documentation: idle disconnect, touchpad boundaries, battery decode, the Bluetooth disconnect IOCTL, DualSense rumble-mode bits, the gyro jitter curve, the stick-as-mouse scale and the Bluetooth output-report CRC seed. Its virtual keyboard’s key table guided PadForge’s. GPL-3.0-or-later, read as documentation only, no GPL code ships.

data.name: About_WiimoteLibDesc
data.value: Wii IR camera and Balance Board behaviour documentation, by Brian Peek. MIT.

data.name: MovePair_Instructions
data.value: Connect the PlayStation Move or Navigation controller with a USB cable, then click Pair. PadForge writes this PC into the controller, saves the Move's motion calibration and registers it. When it finishes, unplug the controller and press its PS button to connect over Bluetooth.

data.name: Nfc_RegisteredFormat
data.value: Registered "{0}". Tap another tag to add more.

data.name: DeviceType_AnalogKeyboard
data.value: Analogue Keyboard

data.name: Dashboard_HeadTrackingDesc
data.value: Reads a head pose from OpenTrack’s UDP output, from the FreeTrack 2.0 shared memory or from a VR headset through an OpenXR runtime, and exposes it as six axes on a Head Tracker device: yaw, pitch, roll and the three translations. Map head yaw to a stick axis to look around while both thumbs stay on the buttons.

data.name: Dashboard_HeadTrackingRotationRange_Tooltip
data.value: Head rotation that moves the yaw, pitch and roll axes to full deflection.

data.name: Dashboard_HeadTrackingTranslationRange_Tooltip
data.value: Head travel that moves the X, Y and Z axes to full deflection.

data.name: Dashboard_HeadTrackingAxisRangesDesc
data.value: Set one axis on its own. Zero follows the range above. Rotation is in degrees, travel in centimetres.

data.name: Handheld_Intro
data.value: Press the hidden button once when asked. PadForge watches the keyboard, the mouse, every vendor report and every system event on this machine, and records whichever one the button changes.

data.name: Handheld_RegisteredFormat
data.value: Registered "{0}". Start again to learn another.

data.name: MapKeyLights_Intro
data.value: PadForge lights one key light at a time. Press the key under the lit light to name it. The names are kept for every keyboard of this model, so Key Colours and the key colour macros reach the right keys.

data.name: Pad_MouseGestures_Desc
data.value: Hold the gesture button, flick, and one action fires when you release: left, right, up, down or a plain click below the flick distance. Map the five gestures on the Mappings tab or use them as macro triggers.

data.name: Pad_MouseGestures_Enabled_Tooltip
data.value: Arms the gesture recogniser for this mouse on this slot. The gesture button keeps its normal click while gesturing, so pick a side button you do not otherwise map.

data.name: Pad_MouseGestures_Button_Tooltip
data.value: The mouse buttons that arm the recogniser while held. Each selected button carries its own five gestures, so different buttons can drive different actions.

data.name: Pad_MouseGestures_Custom_Tooltip
data.value: Arms the recogniser with a recorded input from any device instead of a mouse button: a key, a gamepad button or an analogue input such as a pedal. Record the input below.

data.name: Pad_MouseGestures_CustomInput_Tooltip
data.value: The input that arms the Custom gesture session while held, recorded from any device on this slot. Buttons and keys arm while pressed. Analogue inputs such as a pedal arm past half travel.

data.name: MacroAction_Type_SetChromaColor
data.value: Set Chroma Colour

data.name: MacroAction_SetChromaColor_Tooltip
data.value: Paints the Razer devices assigned to this virtual controller, and every other Razer device of their kinds, one colour while the action runs.

data.name: MacroAction_SetChromaColor_Hint
data.value: For the duration above, paints this colour on the Razer devices assigned to this virtual controller and on every other Razer device of their kinds, or on every Razer device when the Razer Chroma row is assigned. It overrides any virtual controller’s Lighting tab, then hands the lighting back. To hold the colour for as long as the trigger is held, use While Held with Until Release. When two macros paint at once, the one lower in the list wins, so put a full-press macro below its soft-press twin. When macros on two virtual controllers paint the same kind of Razer device, the smaller player number wins. Needs Razer Synapse running.

data.name: MacroAction_ShowDreamcastScreen_Hint
data.value: Each picture is shown for a second at least, since the adapter keeps every picture it is sent in memory rated for 100,000 writes, which a new picture every second reaches in about a day. Pictures are 48 by 32 black-and-white pixels from a BMP or PNG, a VMU Animator .lcd file or a Dreamcast .vms icon.

data.name: Pad_Lighting_GuideLed_Subtitle
data.value: Brightness of the glowing Guide or Home button. Xbox One and later controllers accept it over USB. The 2015 Steam Controller accepts it on any connection, and all Steam Controllers share one brightness. Switch Pro Controllers and right Joy-Cons (alone, paired or in the charging grip) accept it on any connection.

data.name: Macro_GuideLedBrightness_Hint
data.value: Applies to Xbox controllers over USB, the 2015 Steam Controller and Switch controllers with a Home button LED. Pair two of these actions to flash the LED when a macro starts and restore it when it ends.

data.name: Pad_Combine_StickTrim_Description
data.value: The row's last source is a trim stick. While the other sources hold the trigger, pushing the stick up raises the held level and pulling it down lowers it. Built for fine throttle and brake control on pads without analogue triggers.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_TrimRate_Tooltip
data.value: How fast a fully deflected stick slides the held level, as a percentage of the trigger range per second. 100 sweeps from empty to full in one second.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_MotionRowUnreadNote
data.value: Sticks and buttons are not read on this row. Map them to Motion Pitch, Motion Yaw or Motion Roll, then remove them here.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_TrimReset_Tooltip
data.value: When ticked, releasing the trigger snaps the held level back to 100% so the next press starts full. Unticked keeps the trimmed level across releases until you adjust it again.

data.name: Settings_CommunityConfigsDesc
data.value: Browse community-made Steam Input controller configurations and translate them into PadForge profiles. PadForge connects directly to Steam's servers only when you search, open a config or check your imported configs for updates. It sends your search text, the ids of the games, configs and creators involved, and PadForge's version. The anonymous Steam logon also sends your Windows version and a machine id made from hashes of your Windows installation ID, network adapter addresses and boot disk serial. No telemetry, no third-party service, no Steam account.

data.value: Zeroes the pad's accumulated gyro aim references on press. Smoothing history clears, the Motion Lean neutral re-captures, the gravity estimate re-seeds from the controller's current pose, and the turn the Motion Pitch, Yaw and Roll rows built is undone.

data.name: Menu_Fire_TouchRelease_Desc
data.value: Fires once when you let go: lift your finger off the pad, or let the stick snap back to centre while a cell is highlighted.

data.name: Menu_Cells_Tip
data.value: How many cells the menu has. For a radial ring this counts the ring only; the centre cell is separate.

data.name: Menu_HasCenter_Tip
data.value: Adds a centre cell, selected while the stick or finger rests inside the Engage Deadzone.

data.name: Menu_Deadzone_Tip
data.value: For sticks, how far to push before the menu opens and ring cells highlight. On radial menus it is also the centre region for both sticks and touchpads: inside it, the centre cell is selected when one exists.

data.name: Menu_Position_Tip
data.value: Where the overlay's centre sits on screen, as a percentage. 50 and 50 is the middle.

data.name: Menu_Scale_Tip
data.value: Overlay size, as a percentage of its normal size.

data.name: Menu_CustomAxis_Tip
data.value: Record any two axes to steer the menu: push past the Engage Deadzone to open it. This is how joysticks, wheels and other non-gamepad devices host menus.

data.name: Dashboard_OverlaysDescription
data.value: On-screen indicators PadForge shows while you play. Turning one off never changes behaviour, only whether it is announced.

data.name: Pad_RumbleAudio_Card_Desc
data.value: Works with Xbox, DualShock 3, DualShock 4 / DualSense and Nintendo Switch Pro virtual controllers, plus Extended virtual controllers with force feedback, such as racing wheels, and the Steam Deck Controller (Composite). Game feedback and Test Rumble play through the audio output. Macro rumble stays on the controller.

data.name: About_HandheldCompanionDesc
data.value: 3D controller models (Xbox 360, Steam Deck) and the 3D view's model and animation code, by CasperH2O, Lesueur Benjamin, trippyone. Also the reference for the Steam Deck report and haptic decode, the Steam Controller (2015) power-off report, the handheld daemon watch list, the update check timing and the hub port cycle, 500 ms apart, that reconnects a hidden USB controller so programs that opened it first lose it. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

data.name: Starter_Desktop_Description
data.value: Run Windows from the couch. Cursor, scroll and clicks on the triggers.

data.name: Starter_Emulation_Description
data.value: RetroArch and its frontends. Hold Back for save states, loading and speed.

data.name: Starter_Intro
data.value: Ready-made profiles for a whole genre. Pick one, assign any controller and play. Saving adds an ordinary profile you can edit.

data.name: Status_StarterImported_Format
data.value: Added starter profile "{0}".

data.name: Starter_Strategy_Description
data.value: RTS, 4X and city builders. Camera on one stick, cursor on the other.

data.name: Starter_Isometric_Description
data.value: Party RPGs and turn-based tactics. Pause, inventory and a hotbar.

data.name: Starter_Media_Description
data.value: Playback, seeking and a cursor for the ten-foot experience.

data.name: Starter_Racing_Description
data.value: Calmer steering and finer control near centre, on any pad.

data.name: Pad_Audio_CrossfeedCut_Tooltip
data.value: Crossover frequency. Below it the channels blend towards mono, above it they stay separated, so a lower cutoff crossfeeds less.

data.name: Pad_Audio_EqHowTo
data.value: For a correction matched to your headphones: open autoeq.app, choose your model, pick Custom Parametric Eq and download it, then Import from File. The Graphic Eq download has no filter lines and will not be imported.

data.name: Pad_Audio_LimiterCeiling_Tooltip
data.value: Highest level the limiter allows through, as a percentage of full scale.

data.name: About_MouseArtDesc
data.value: Mouse artwork in the Keyboard + Mouse visualisation, by Igor Budzhak. MIT.

data.name: Macro_PressureScaledRate_Tooltip
data.value: The repeat rate follows how hard the selected analogue source is pressed. A light press repeats at the Slow Interval, a full press at the Interval above, and everything between blends smoothly.

data.name: Macro_PressureTurboHint
data.value: Pick the analogue source the rate follows: a trigger, a DualShock 3 pressure axis (Axis 6-15) or the stick this macro triggers on. When the source is the trigger’s own axis, the pressure follows the trigger’s direction, so a stick reads 0 at centre and 1 at full push either way.

data.name: Settings_AssignOfferDesc
data.value: When a device connects while a virtual controller's page is open, PadForge can offer to assign it there. Nothing is assigned until you click Assign. Keyboards, mice, touchpads and media keys are never offered.

data.name: Voice_ConfidenceTooltip
data.value: How sure the recogniser must be before a phrase fires. Raise it if random speech triggers macros, lower it if your phrases are missed.

data.name: Voice_Registered_Format
data.value: Registered "{0}". Say it to fire its button, and bind macros to it on the Pad page.

data.name: MacroAction_VoiceListenWhileHeld_Tooltip
data.value: Push to talk for Voice Macros: while this macro is held, the recogniser listens. Set Listening to Push to Talk in Manage Voice Macros.

data.name: About_MingwRuntimeDesc
data.value: libgcc_s_seh-1.dll, libstdc++-6.dll and libwinpthread-1.dll, the native runtime the Vosk recogniser needs, shipped inside the x64 build. GPL-3.0-or-later with the GCC Runtime Library Exception, and for winpthreads MIT, with BSD 3-Clause for the parts derived from Lockless Inc.'s Posix Threads library. The ARM64 build's libvosk.dll carries its own runtime: mingw-w64 and winpthreads, and LLVM's libc++, libunwind and compiler-rt under Apache-2.0 with LLVM Exceptions.

data.name: About_TritonLibDesc
data.value: Steam Controller 2026 PCM haptics stream (reports 0x86, 0x88 and 0x44), by Pixel1011 (Apache-2.0), FamBoy32-dev (MIT), iczero (MIT) and ga2mer. Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_LogitechLedRefsDesc
data.value: Engine entry points, calling convention and zone layout behind Logitech lighting through G HUB, read from Artemis.Plugins (PolyForm Noncommercial), Aurora (MIT), LogiLed2Corsair (MIT), Logitech-LED (GPL-2.0), logitech-led-sdk-rs (MIT OR Apache-2.0) and RGB.NET (LGPL-2.1). PadForge loads G HUB's own engine and ships no Logitech code.

data.name: About_OpenXrRefsDesc
data.value: The runtime interface, structure layout and registry keys behind headset and motion controller input, read from the Khronos OpenXR-SDK headers (Apache-2.0) and cross-checked against VirtualDesktop-OpenXR (MIT). PadForge talks to your own installed runtime and ships no Khronos code.

data.name: About_PeripheralOutputRefsDesc
data.value: The Logitech HID++ haptic, lighting, pairing and battery frames, read from Solaar (GPL-2.0-or-later), libratbag (MIT), LiveHaptics, OpenLogi (0BSD and MIT OR Apache-2.0), the OpenLogi docs, keyleds (GPL-3.0-or-later), g810-led and g810-led-resources (GPL-3.0), rigdeck (GPL-3.0-or-later), OpenGHub (MIT) and g915x-heatmap (MIT), with notes from OpenRGB-Fixed (GPL-2.0-or-later) and HaloDaemon-plugins. The Razer product IDs and lighting reports, read from OpenRazer (GPL-2.0-or-later) and OpenRGB (GPL-2.0-or-later) and checked against uncoil (GPL-3.0-or-later), OpenSynapse (MIT), openrazer-win (GPL-2.0-or-later), sanshoku (MIT), razer_test (GPL-3.0-or-later) and razer-life (GPL-2.0-or-later), with the lock those tools share from Aurora (MIT) and LibreHardwareMonitor (MPL-2.0). The SteelSeries product IDs and lighting reports, read from OpenRGB and rivalcfg (WTFPL) and checked against SignalRGB's plugins, Aerox_5 (MIT), apex-3-tkl (MIT), ApexCtl (LGPL-3.0), SteelSeriesControl (GPL-3.0), rival310-re (LGPL-3.0), Cricetus-Imperator (MIT) and Wine (LGPL-2.1-or-later). The HID LampArray reports, read from the USB-IF HID Usage Tables, Microsoft's Dynamic Lighting documentation and its samples ArduinoHidForWindows and RP2040MacropadHidSample (MIT), and checked against lampctl (MIT OR Apache-2.0), hid-rgb-ctl, keybackcon, mistel-lights, CaYaLight, hp-omen-35l-rgb, mac-dynamic-lighting, aura-loq and Apex3TklDynamicLighting (all MIT), acer-predator-helios-rgb (GPL-2.0-only) and crosrgbkblight. The iFeel buzz report, read from iFeel, the Linux iFeel driver (GPL-2.0-or-later) and Logitech-iFeel-Vibration-POC, with a descriptor rule from the Linux kernel (GPL-2.0-or-later) and the strength scale from Logitech's MouseWare 9.80 driver. The tactile and colour handlers from the GameSense SDK. Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_PortMidiRtMidiDesc
data.value: The WinMM call sequences behind the legacy MIDI API: opening a port, sending to it and closing it. Read from PortMidi (MIT, by Ross Bencina, Phil Burk and Roger B. Dannenberg) and RtMidi (MIT-style RtMidi licence, by Gary P. Scavone). Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_AnalogKeyboardRefs
data.value: HallJoy, Soup and AnalogSense

data.name: About_AnalogKeyboardRefsDesc
data.value: Analogue keyboard input ports HallJoy’s keyboard routes, key tables and model catalogues to C# (AGPL-3.0, PashOK7) and follows Soup and the AnalogSense JavaScript SDK (MIT, Calamity, Inc.), checked against the Wooting Analog SDK (MPL-2.0). Other keyboards follow AnalogKeys (MIT, Nisayera), KeyAxis (MIT, RigZeeel), HallEffectAnalogMapper (MIT, Ricards Mironovs), libhmk and hmkconf (GPL-3.0-or-later, peppapighs), and the Soup forks of DenkiSuki, LeiterConsulting and paysdelest (MIT). Report formats and key tables also come from Razer’s Synapse Web and NuPhy’s NuPhyIO configurators, OpenRazer (GPL-2.0-or-later), Abbytech’s razer-analog-keyboard, TinyUSB (MIT) and Sainan’s capture notes.

data.name: About_BlissBoxRefsDesc
data.value: The Bliss-Box API behind Read Bliss-Box Adapters, read from Bliss-Box LLC’s API Tool (BSD-style, redistribution free of charge) and DeviceBuddy (source available, Bliss-Box LLC), with button names from the Bliss-Box files in SteveFox1620’s retroarch-joypad-autoconfig fork, Controller Pak checksums checked against libdragon (Unlicense), and the PlayStation pad reply from psx-spx and Linux’s psxpad-spi driver (GPL-2.0-or-later). Controller names and support notes also come from Bliss-Box LLC’s compatibility list, and the adapters’ behaviour was checked against their firmware. Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: Menu_Fire_Click_LayerHold_Desc
data.value: Holds the highlighted cell's binding while the Click Input is held. A highlighted radial centre can fire while the stick rests.

data.name: Menu_Fire_Always_LayerHold_Desc
data.value: Holds the binding while its cell is highlighted. A radial centre can fire immediately when the layer opens.

data.name: Menu_Fire_ButtonPairGrid_Desc
data.value: Direction presses step through the cells and fire each newly selected cell. This hotbar behaviour does not use Fire Mode or Click Input.

data.name: Pad_SteeringAngleRumble_Description
data.value: Adds continuous rumble as the selected virtual stick axis moves away from centre. Uses the mapped output from all assigned sources. With Split by Direction, negative movement drives the left motor and positive movement the right. Left Motor or Right Motor puts both directions on that one motor. For Xbox and PlayStation output with rumble devices. Native wheel force feedback is excluded.

data.value: Reset Centre Deadzone (2%)

data.name: About_NefconDesc
data.value: HidHide's install tool, by Nefarius. Its ARM64 build installs the HidHide driver on Windows on ARM. It links Argh!, colorwin, easyloggingpp, Microsoft Detours, scope_guard, the Windows Implementation Libraries and neflib. MIT.

data.name: About_Kaldi
data.value: Kaldi, OpenFst, OpenBLAS and CLAPACK

data.name: About_KaldiDesc
data.value: The speech decoder, transducer library and linear algebra inside libvosk.dll. Kaldi and OpenFst: Apache-2.0. OpenBLAS and CLAPACK: BSD 3-Clause, with separate notices for GotoBLAS2 inside OpenBLAS and for the f2c runtime.

data.name: About_AntiMicroXDesc
data.value: Strategy and desktop starter-profile layouts, and the turbo behaviour the pressure-scaled turbo avoids. GPL-3.0-or-later, read as documentation only, no GPL code ships.

data.name: About_AutoHotkeyDesc
data.value: SendInput techniques behind Text Block macros and the keyboard chord hook: Unicode typing, batch limits, the Win-key mask key and tagged injected input. GPL-2.0-or-later, read as documentation only, no GPL code ships.

data.name: About_Ds4MapperTestDesc
data.value: DualShock 4 battery ranges, touchpad haptic pulse timing and intensity steps, and touchpad fling behaviour. GPL-3.0, read as documentation only, no GPL code ships.

data.name: About_Ds4WindowsHbashtonDesc
data.value: DualSense audio volume ranges, signed 8-bit haptic samples and the combined Bluetooth transport layout. GPL-3.0, read as documentation only, no GPL code ships.

data.name: About_HadoDesc
data.value: 3D models of the DualShock 4, DualSense, DualSense Edge, Xbox Series and Switch 2 Pro Controller, bought on CGTrader. CGTrader Royalty Free License.

data.name: About_HidapiDesc
data.value: The HID layer compiled into the bundled SDL3.dll, by Alan Ott, Signal 11 Software. BSD-style licence.

data.name: About_IconSourcesDesc
data.value: The flame glyph from Material Design Icons (Pictogrammers, Apache-2.0), the generic gamepad icon from Ionicons (Ionic, MIT), the Extended joystick from Jam Icons (Michael Amprimo, MIT) and the Xbox and PlayStation icons from SVG Repo, under the licence on each icon's page.

data.name: About_Jc2MouseDesc
data.value: Joy-Con 2 optical mouse counters and wraparound deltas behind Mouse Motion X and Y, by coffincolors, Frano and moutella. MIT. Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_VcRuntimeDesc
data.value: The C++ runtime SDL3.dll needs (msvcp140.dll, vcruntime140.dll and, in the x64 build, vcruntime140_1.dll), shipped unmodified inside PadForge. Microsoft Visual Studio licence terms.

data.name: About_SwitchResearchDesc
data.value: Joy-Con and Pro Controller HID, HD rumble and home LED notes, by dekuNukem, with ndeadly's switch2_controller_research for the Switch 2. Read for protocol facts only.

data.name: About_PsmoveapiDesc
data.value: PlayStation Move report layouts, sensor calibration and the EXT accessory handshake, by Thomas Perl, cross-checked against the moveonpc wiki. PadForge's implementation is original C#. BSD 2-Clause.

data.name: About_SipSorceryDesc
data.value: The STUN message layout and XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS decode behind Remote Link's NAT traversal, vendored from its C# source, by Aaron Clauson. BSD 3-Clause, with the use restriction in section 2 of its licence.

data.name: About_SpaceMouseRefsDesc
data.value: 3Dconnexion report layout, device table and axis scale, read from hid.spacemouse (MIT), PySpaceMouse (MIT), spacemouse by AndunHH (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) and spacenavd (GPL-3.0-or-later). Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_SteamControllerRefsDesc
data.value: Swipe-haptic ticks, report 0x42 button bits, the power-off command and the dongle relay, read from OpenPuck (AGPL-3.0), sc2-research (MIT), steam_controller_tools (GPL-2.0) and SteamlessController (MIT). Documentation only, no GPL or AGPL code ships.

data.name: About_TouchmoteDesc
data.value: Wii Remote IR pointer behaviour: dot-pair midpoint, margins, sensor-bar offset, smoothing and the FPS Mouse curve, with the Ryochan7, Suegrini and Trihy forks. GPL-3.0, read as documentation only, no GPL code ships.

data.name: About_WheelRefsDesc
data.value: Native force feedback and RPM shift LED reports for Fanatec, Thrustmaster and Logitech wheels, read from hid-fanatecff (GPL-2.0), hid-tmff2 (GPL-2.0-or-later), new-lg4ff (GPL-2.0-or-later), oversteer (GPL-3.0) and thrustmaster-led-linux (GPL-3.0), and cross-checked against the SimHub LED plugin by prodigal.knight (MIT) and tm-bt-led (MIT). Documentation only, no GPL code ships.

data.name: About_ArcadeIoRefsDesc
data.value: The protocols behind the SDL fork's drivers for Namco and Konami arcade I/O boards and JVS boards, read from arcade-docs (WTFPL), bemanitools (Unlicense), Dolphin (GPL-2.0-or-later), ITAIKO-firmware (MIT), JoypadOS (Apache-2.0), jvsio (BSD-3-Clause), MAME (BSD-3-Clause), OpenITG (StepMania licence), p4io-mdxfdrv (GPL-3.0), RPCS3 (GPL-2.0) and TaikoZucchini (MIT). Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_BleControllerRefsDesc
data.value: The protocols behind the SDL fork's Bluetooth LE drivers for the Poke Ball Plus, Daydream, Gear VR, Oculus Go, Guitar Hero Live iOS, Zwift and Myo controllers, read from Access-GearVR-Controller-from-PC (Apache-2.0), daydream-catcher, daydream-controller.js (MIT), daydream2hid (Apache-2.0), dl-myo (GPL-3.0), find-a-cig (MIT), gear_vr_controller (MIT), gearVRC (MIT), gearvr-controller (MIT), gearvr-controller-webbluetooth (GPL-3.0), GHLtarUtility (GPL-3.0), ghlioscon (MIT), hardfault.life, jsyang.ca, makinolo.com, myo-bluetooth (Apache-2.0), myo-raw (MIT), OculusGo-Air-Mouse-4-macOS (MIT), PlasticBand (CC BY-SA 4.0), pokeball-plus-4-windows, pokeball-plus-mouse (Apache-2.0), PokeBall-Plus-Controller-Driver-App-Mac, PokeballPlus-4-PC (MIT), pyomyo (MIT), qdomyos-zwift (GPL-3.0), Santroller (GPL-3.0), SwiftControl (noncommercial), Zephyr (Apache-2.0) and zwiftplay. Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_RfcommIcadeRefsDesc
data.value: The protocols behind the SDL fork's drivers for the MOGA, Zeemote, BGP100 and Phonejoy pads and the ION iCade, read from android-bluez-ime (LGPL-2.1-or-later), flatlib.jp, iCade-iOS (MIT), Linux (GPL-2.0-or-later), MogaSerial (MIT), moga-uinput (MIT), ZeeClient (MIT), zeemoted (GPL-3.0-or-later) and zeemouse. Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_HidDeviceRefsDesc
data.value: The reports behind the SDL fork's drivers for the Speed Force Wireless, PhoenixRC adapter, SideWinder Game Voice, P5 Glove, Dream Cheeky drum kit, OCZ NIA, Gametrak, Rift DK1, Windows Mixed Reality controllers, SteelSeries Nimbus and Prodikeys, read from acassis.wordpress.com, drwho.virtadpt.net, Foculus Rift Tracker, GameTrak-Liberation (MIT), libgametrak (GPL-2.0-or-later), libp5glove (LGPL-2.1-or-later), Linux (GPL-2.0), Linux VR Adventures wiki, marcusfolkesson.se, MFIGamepadFeeder (MIT), ml-driver (GPL-2.0), Monado (BSL-1.0), new-lg4ff (GPL-2.0-or-later), nia_reaction_lab, nia4linux (GPL-2.0), Oculus SDK (Oculus VR SDK License 2.0), OpenHMD (BSL-1.0), P5 Glove USB Packet Format, PCSX2 (GPL-3.0-or-later), pynia (MIT), Scratchpad wiki (CC BY-SA), seewald.at, VRPN (BSL-1.0), weewx (GPL-3.0) and WiiBrew. Documentation only, except the OpenHMD and Monado code listed separately.

data.name: About_InstrumentRefsDesc
data.value: The protocols behind the SDL fork's drivers for Wii Remote instrument and tablet extensions, Guitar Hero Live dongles, Rock Band 3 Pro instruments and PS3 peripherals, read from AutoCalibrationRB, brandonw.net, Dolphin (GPL-2.0-or-later), GHLtarUtility (GPL-3.0), GHLtarUtility by Sera486 (GPL-3.0), hid-ghlive-dkms (GPL-3.0), JoypadOS (Apache-2.0), Linux (GPL-2.0), NintendoExtensionCtrl (LGPL-3.0-or-later), PlasticBand (CC BY-SA 4.0), raphnet.net, rb3_keytar (MIT), RB4InstrumentMapper (MIT), RPCS3 (GPL-2.0), Santroller (GPL-3.0), uDrawTablet, WiiBrew, WiitarThing (MIT) and xpad by paroj (GPL-2.0-or-later). Documentation only, no code ships.

data.value: The protocols behind the SDL fork's serial drivers for six-axis controllers, gamepads, flight sticks, RC transmitters, flight panels and ergometers, read from Async.fi, hidsporb, JoypadOS (Apache-2.0), KettlerBLE (MIT), kettlerUSB2BLE (MIT), libsball by John E. data.value: The protocols behind the SDL fork's drivers for the Intel Wireless Series base station, the Xbox 360 Big Button receiver, the CH Products Multi-Function Panel, the Ergodex DX1, the TrackIR 2 and 3, and Tacx trainer head units, read from antifier (MIT), chmfp (GPL-3.0-or-later), dx1-studio (GPL-3.0), ergodex-dx1-linux (GPL-3.0), fortius_1942 (GPL-2.0-or-later), FortiusANT (GPL-3.0), intel-wings (GPL-2.0), JoypadOS (Apache-2.0), linuxtrack (MIT), t19xx_usb (GPL-3.0), ttyT1941 (GPL-3.0) and xbox360bb (GPL-2.0-or-later). data.name: About_TrainControllerRefsDesc
data.value: The protocols behind the SDL fork's drivers for Densha de GO!, Multi Train, Train Mascon and Master Controller train controllers, read from amy.hi-ho.ne.jp by Takatani, bvets.net by Mackoy, ConToJREts, ddgo-pnp-controller (GPL-3.0), OpenBVE (BSD-2-Clause), PCSX2 (GPL-3.0-or-later), Qiita by kazuhidet, RPCS3 (GPL-2.0), Scrapbox by p4ken and Train Controller Database. Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_XboxControllerRefsDesc
data.value: The protocols behind the SDL fork's original Xbox, Steel Battalion, Xbox 360 chatpad and Xbox 360 uDraw drivers, and the Xbox 360 receivers PadForge binds to Windows' own driver, read from brandonw.net, Chatpad Super Driver (MIT), Cxbx-Reloaded (GPL-2.0-or-later), euc.jp by ITO Takayuki, JoypadOS (Apache-2.0), libSteelBattalion, libsteelbat, Linux (GPL-2.0-or-later), ogx360 (GPL-3.0-or-later), s-config.com, SBC (MIT), Spivey's Corner, steel-battalion-net (LGPL-3.0), SteelBattalionController (Apache-2.0), SteelBattalionDriver (GPL-3.0), SteelBattalionMapper (GPL-3.0-or-later), tusb_xinput (MIT), uDrawTablet, Xb2XInput (GPL-3.0), xb360ChatpadToKM (GPL-3.0), xbox360wirelesschatpad, xboxdevwiki, xboxdrv (GPL-3.0-or-later) and xemu (LGPL-2.0-or-later). Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_GameModRefsDesc
data.value: The UDP instructions, replies, port files and trigger effect bytes behind Game Mods, read from Paliverse’s official DSX v3.1 and DualSenseX v2 mod examples, both versions of DualSenseY and DualSense4Rockstar (no licence published), DSZ and pydualsense (MIT), and the Wujek Dualsense API and the DSX server in hbashton’s DS4Windows fork (GPL-3.0). Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_Ds4HeadsetRefsDesc
data.value: The headphone and speaker routing, volume ceilings, microphone framing and report mode behind DualShock 4 Bluetooth audio, read from DS4-Sound-Link (MIT), ds4mac (GPL-2.0), ds4drv (MIT) and hbashton’s DS4Windows fork (GPL-3.0), with the SBC decoder’s synthesis windows checked against Google’s libsbc (Apache-2.0), and the USB headsets of the second model and Sony’s adapter read from DJm00n’s ControllersInfo descriptor dumps (no licence published) and linux-hardware.org’s LsUSB probes (CC BY 4.0). Documentation only, no code ships.

data.name: About_KeyboardScreenRefsDesc
data.value: The libraries, frames and keys behind keyboard screens, read from Logitech’s LCD and Arx Control SDKs and Mad Catz’s S.T.R.I.K.E. 7 SDK, cross-checked against logitech-lcd (MIT or Apache-2.0), dcspy (MIT), foo_logitech_lcd (LGPL-2.1), LogitechStuff and ArxWidgetManager (no licence published), Linux’s hid-lg-g15 driver (GPL-2.0-or-later), libg15, G15Interface and lcdproc (GPL-2.0), gnome15 (GPL-3.0) and G19USB (Apache-2.0). PadForge loads Logitech Gaming Software’s libraries and the Strike7API.dll you download or choose and ships no code from any of them.

data.name: About_FalconRefsDesc
data.value: The library calls, feels and game forces behind Novint Falcon support, read from Force Dimension’s SDK headers, documentation and examples, with the Joystick feel from FalconJoystick and the Aim feel and rumble from FalconJoyForce (both by Cyclops-11B, no licence published), checked against CHAI3D (BSD 3-Clause) and libnifalcon (BSD). PadForge loads the Force Dimension library you install, since its licence grants no right to redistribute it, and ships no code from any of them.

data.name: Settings_KeyboardScreens_Desc
data.value: Draws on the screens built into Logitech's GamePanel keyboards and the Mad Catz S.T.R.I.K.E. 7, and on a phone through Logitech Arx Control: the profile, a clock, play time, a stopwatch, a picture or a DualShock 4 or DualSense lightbar's colour. Each screen gets its own row on the Devices page, where you set what it shows. The keys beside a screen are its row's buttons.

data.name: Settings_KeyboardScreensTooltip
data.value: Draws on the Logitech G15, G15 v2, G510, G13, Z-10, GamePanel and G19 screens, on Arx Control and on the Mad Catz S.T.R.I.K.E. 7. While Logitech Gaming Software runs, PadForge draws through it. Without it, PadForge writes the monochrome screens over HID and binds WinUSB to the G19's screen interface. Turning this off gives the G19's screen back to Windows.

data.name: KeyboardScreens_Configure_Color
data.value: Colour Screen…

data.name: KeyboardScreens_DownloadStrike7_Tooltip
data.value: Downloads Mad Catz's S.T.R.I.K.E. 7 SDK from AIDA64's server, checks it against its known SHA-256 and keeps only the 64-bit Strike7API.dll in PadForge's temporary folder.

data.name: KeyboardScreens_InstallVc2008_Tooltip
data.value: Downloads Microsoft's Visual C++ 2008 SP1 Redistributable for 64-bit Windows, which Strike7API.dll needs, checks Microsoft's signature on it and installs it.

data.name: KeyboardScreen_Hint_Stopwatch
data.value: The screen shows the stopwatch, which the Stopwatch macro starts, pauses and resets. Every screen shows the same stopwatch.

data.name: KeyboardScreen_Hint_Lightbar
data.value: The screen shows the colour of the lightbar on the DualShock 4 or DualSense in the lowest slot this screen feeds, or in the lowest slot of all when it feeds none. A monochrome screen shows its brightness as a dot pattern. Until a colour reaches a lightbar, PadForge shows nothing.

data.name: MacroAction_ShowKeyboardScreen_Hint
data.value: Pictures are fitted to the screen: 160 by 43 black and white pixels on a monochrome screen, 320 by 240 on the G19's and 480 by 320 for Arx Control and the S.T.R.I.K.E. 7. A Screen Overlay keeps each picture's own shape, up to 800 pixels on its longer side. A tenth of a second is the shortest frame time. A repeat count of 0 keeps playing until another Show Keyboard Screen or Keyboard Screen Mode macro.

data.name: Status_FalconDriverPackageMissing_Format
data.value: Force Dimension's Falcon driver package, or its catalogue, is missing: {0}. Reinstall Force Dimension's SDK.

data.name: Pad_Falcon_Feel_Tooltip
data.value: Joystick: the handle's position is the stick, and a spring pulls it back to centre. Aim: the handle's motion moves the stick, and holding the handle against the wall at its edge keeps turning.

data.value: Centring Spring

data.value: Reset Centring Spring

data.name: Pad_Falcon_KickButton_Tooltip
data.value: While this grip button is held, and for a quarter second after, the game's rumble kicks the handle towards you. Rumble at other times shakes the handle.

data.value: Lights keys in a colour on the keyboards and other devices this virtual controller lights: steady, fading, or counting down one key at a time.

data.name: MacroAction_ClearKeyColors_Tooltip
data.value: Ends the Set Key Colours actions running on this virtual controller that light one of the keys picked here, or every one when none is picked.

data.name: MacroAction_SetKeyColors_Hint
data.value: The action lights the same keys on every keyboard this virtual controller lights, over the colours its Lighting tab gives them. The numbers show the order picked. Countdown turns the keys off one at a time, the last one picked first, so pick 1 to 0 for a cooldown on the number row. A keyboard or mouse lights only while its Control This Device’s Lighting is on.

data.name: Dashboard_ScreenOverlayDescription
data.value: Shows a picture, a timer, the time or a lightbar's colour above other windows, with no keyboard screen needed. While another program is in front, clicks pass through it. While PadForge is in front, drag it with the right mouse button and size it from its corner.

data.name: KeyboardScreen_Hint_Lightbar_Overlay
data.value: The overlay shows the colour of the lightbar on the DualShock 4 or DualSense in the slot you choose here, or in the lowest slot with a colour. Until a colour reaches a lightbar, it shows nothing.
